global_system_instructions.description: Standing rules that apply to every answer. GP serves the text in protected-prompts.defaultGlobalSystemInstructions. Fixed on the managed and on-device lanes; the user's own text is substituted only when they are running their own key.

prompt_system_instructions.description: GP's instruction for this specific call type. Authored by GP on every lane. Placed after global instructions so it is the more proximate instruction when the two disagree.

output_constraints.description: Format rules that survive every other instruction, e.g. the dash prohibition. Own section so it can be revised without touching prompt text.

project_context.description: Project metadata and attached project files.

meeting_context.description: The manifest plus one block per selected meeting, oldest first. See docs/wire-contracts/project-chat-prompt-assembly.md for the block format, which this spec does not change.

rolling_summary.description: The running meeting summary. Changes on a cadence rather than per turn.

context_quilt.description: Context Quilt recall. Ranked per question, so it changes on every turn and is placed last in the system block to keep everything above it cacheable.

reference_text.description: User-attached references for this send. Sent as its own top-level field rather than concatenated, so GP can render it as a separately cached part on lanes that support one.

transcript.description: Live transcript buffer or excerpt. Grows every turn, so it must never sit in the system block.

user_query.description: What the user actually asked. Always last.

copilot_session.note: Order reproduces the shipped systemPromptTemplate exactly, including context_quilt sitting ahead of summary and project. That ordering is not cache-optimal and is a known follow-up; it is left alone here so this spec changes no live behavior.

post_session_analysis.note: The session is over, so the summary is final rather than periodic. It is large and unchanging across the turns of a post-session conversation, which makes it worth having inside the cached prefix instead of behind the boundary.
